Successful Chiller Repair at Waghodia GIDC (Feb 2026)

A comprehensive technical breakdown of how we restored industrial cooling efficiency at Cryogas through advanced diagnostics and component optimization.

Successful Chiller Repair at Waghodia GIDC is not just about fixing a machine; it is about restoring the heartbeat of an industrial facility. In February 2026, our team at Atlas Aircons undertook a critical project at Cryogas, a prominent facility located in the bustling industrial hub of Waghodia GIDC. This case study details the meticulous process we employed to diagnose, repair, and optimize a compromised chiller system, ensuring it met the rigorous demands of modern industrial processing.

Industrial chillers are robust machines, but they are susceptible to wear, tear, and environmental factors. When a system fails, the downtime can be costly. Our intervention at Cryogas highlights the importance of expert diagnostics and precision engineering in the HVAC sector. By focusing on quality replacement parts—specifically Danfoss compressors—and thorough cleaning protocols like Nitrogen and CTC flushing, we delivered a result that exceeded client expectations.

Figure 1: Technician assessing the chiller unit at the industrial site.

The Challenge: Critical System Failure at Cryogas

The project began with an urgent service call from the maintenance division at Cryogas in Waghodia GIDC. The facility managers reported that their process chiller was failing to maintain the required setpoint temperatures, leading to potential production delays. Upon arrival, our lead technician initiated a comprehensive diagnostic protocol.

The initial visual inspection and gauge readings revealed a catastrophic issue: water contamination within the refrigeration circuit. This is one of the most severe failures a chiller can experience. Specifically, water had breached the hermetically sealed areas, entering both the compressor and the condenser.

Further investigation pinpointed the root cause: the cooling coil (compact evaporator coil) had sprung a leak. In a chiller system, the evaporator acts as the heat exchanger where the refrigerant absorbs heat from the process water. When this barrier fails, the high-pressure water forces its way into the low-pressure refrigerant side, circulating moisture throughout the entire system. This “hydro-locking” effect damages mechanical components and creates acidic sludge that corrodes internal surfaces.

Strategic Execution: A Step-by-Step Restoration

Once the diagnosis of a Successful Chiller Repair at Waghodia GIDC was confirmed, we provided a detailed quotation to the Cryogas engineering team. Transparency is a core value at Atlas Aircons; we explained that a simple patch-up would not suffice. The severity of water ingress required a major overhaul to guarantee longevity. Following the approval of the Purchase Order, we commenced the repair work with the following strategic steps:

1. Evaporator Coil Replacement

The source of the failure—the leaked compact evaporator coil—was the first component to be addressed. Repairing an old, leaked coil is often a temporary fix that leads to recurring issues. Therefore, we opted for a full replacement. We sourced a high-efficiency, corrosion-resistant compact evaporator coil designed to withstand the specific thermal loads of the Cryogas facility. This ensured that the heat exchange process would be efficient and leak-proof for years to come.

2. Compressor Replacement: Upgrading to Danfoss

Water inside a compressor is a death sentence for the motor windings and the mechanical valves. The existing compressor was compromised beyond repair. To ensure the reliability of this Successful Chiller Repair at Waghodia GIDC, we selected a brand-new Danfoss 5.5 TR Compressor. Danfoss is a global leader in climate solutions, known for compressors that offer:

  • High Energy Efficiency: Reducing operational electricity costs for the client.
  • Robust Durability: Capable of handling fluctuating industrial loads.
  • Low Noise Operation: improving the working environment at the GIDC plant.

(Note: For larger industrial applications requiring significantly higher capacity, we also specialize in installing and servicing robust units like the Emerson ZP 235 KCE 20.0 TR Compressor.)

Danfoss 5.5 TR Compressor Installed

3. Deep System Cleaning: Nitrogen and CTC Flushing

Installing new parts into a dirty system is a recipe for failure. The residual moisture and acid from the previous burnout had to be completely eliminated. We employed a dual-stage flushing process:

  • CTC Flushing: We circulated Carbon Tetrachloride (CTC) and specialized cleaning agents through the copper piping and condenser. This solvent effectively dissolved the sludge, oil contaminants, and carbon deposits left behind by the water intrusion.
  • Nitrogen Flushing: Following the solvent clean, we purged the entire system with high-pressure dry Nitrogen. Nitrogen is an inert gas that does not react with copper or oil. It acts as a “broom,” sweeping away any remaining solvent and absorbing trace moisture. This step is crucial for achieving a deep vacuum later in the process.

4. Air Drier Replacement and Final Commissioning

The final line of defense against moisture is the filter drier. We replaced the saturated unit with a high-capacity air drier. Once the mechanical work was complete, we pulled a deep vacuum to 500 microns to ensure the system was dehydrated. We then charged the system with the precise amount of refrigerant specified by the manufacturer.

Pros and Cons of Component Replacement vs. System Overhaul

In industrial scenarios like the one at Waghodia GIDC, clients often ask if they should repair the unit or buy a new one. Here is why our approach of major component replacement was the winning strategy for Cryogas.

PROS of Our Repair Strategy
  • ✓ Cost Effectiveness: Replacing the compressor and coil is significantly cheaper than purchasing a brand-new industrial chiller setup.
  • ✓ Minimized Downtime: Sourcing parts and installing them took less time than the lead time required for manufacturing and shipping a new chiller unit.
  • ✓ Upgrade Potential: By using a Danfoss 5.5 TR compressor, we effectively upgraded the unit’s performance compared to its original specs.
  • ✓ Environmental Safety: Proper reclamation of gases and disposal of oil prevents environmental damage.
CONS of Delaying Repair
  • ✖ Risk of Total Failure: Had the water sat in the system longer, corrosion could have destroyed the condenser shell, rendering the unit scrap.
  • ✖ Higher Energy Bills: A failing compressor draws excessive amps, spiking electricity costs for the GIDC facility.
  • ✖ Production Quality Loss: Inconsistent cooling affects the quality of the end product in manufacturing.

The Outcome: 100% Client Satisfaction

After the rigorous flushing, part replacement, and gas charging, the chiller was restarted. The results were immediate. The suction and discharge pressures stabilized within the optimal range for the Danfoss 5.5 TR compressor. The cooling coil efficiently dropped the water temperature to the desired setpoint within minutes.

To demonstrate our confidence in this Successful Chiller Repair at Waghodia GIDC, we provided a comprehensive 1-Year Guarantee on our workmanship and the replaced components. The engineering team at Cryogas expressed their complete satisfaction with the professionalism, technical depth, and speed of our service.

Technical Deep Dive: The Importance of the Danfoss 5.5 TR Compressor

In the context of this Successful Chiller Repair at Waghodia GIDC, the choice of the Danfoss 5.5 TR compressor was pivotal. Danfoss scroll compressors are engineered for excellence. Unlike reciprocating compressors, scroll technology utilizes two interleaving scrolls to pump refrigerant. This design has fewer moving parts, resulting in higher reliability and lower vibration.

For the Cryogas application, the 5.5 Ton of Refrigeration (TR) capacity was calculated to match the heat load of the compact evaporator perfectly. An undersized compressor would run continuously, leading to burnout, while an oversized one would cycle too frequently, causing wear. Our precise matching ensured the system operates at its peak efficiency curve.

Understanding the “Water in System” Hazard

Why was the water ingress such a critical issue? In refrigeration chemistry, water reacts with refrigerant and oil to form acid. This acid eats away at the varnish insulation on the motor windings inside the compressor. It also causes copper plating on the bearings, leading to mechanical seizure. The “CTC flushing” we performed stands for Carbon Tetrachloride cleaning (or modern equivalent safety solvents), which is the industry standard for neutralizing this acidity. Without this step, the new Danfoss compressor would have failed within weeks. This attention to chemical detail is what separates a standard mechanic from a specialized HVAC engineer.
